evidence.statement: An LTV visa may be limited to one issuing state; other states are included with consent.
Germany: border admission decisions belong to the competent national border authorities.
France: border police check the conditions of admission; holding a visa does not by itself guarantee entry.
Italy: immigration is assigned to the exclusive legislative competence of the state.
Spain: the national conditions of entry require documents and the prescribed visa through authorised points.
US: CBP makes the admission decision at the port of entry.
India: paragraph 14 establishes permits for foreigners for protected/restricted areas; the territorial list is given separately.
The list of protected areas contains the whole of Arunachal Pradesh and parts of Jammu and Kashmir / Ladakh between the Inner Line and the described international boundary.
China: the travel permit for non-open areas is issued by authorised public security bodies; this is not an independent international admission.
UK: a standard civilian visit is usually up to six months; a passport valid for the duration of the stay or an accepted travel document is required.
Åland: Finnish visa/document requirements apply; the issuing of a regional passport does not create a different citizenship.
Åland: powers concerning aliens remain with Finland.
Åland is in the EU customs territory, but is excluded from the VAT/excise territory; mainland Finland is in all three.
Madeira and Azores in the EU customs/VAT/excise table have the same territorial applicability as Portugal.
The Madeira and Azores airports describe the Portugal/Schengen document regime, but the reference lists are partly outdated.
An ordinary Schengen short-stay visa does not replace the Faroe Islands / Greenland endorsement. The Danish Immigration Service processes the corresponding entry permits.
From 20 March 2026 the corresponding valid Schengen residence permits / qualifying EU-family residence cards give a new exemption for Faroe Islands and Greenland.
Crown Dependencies have their own immigration jurisdictions, with mutual recognition of leave and almost identical visa requirements.
evidence.locator: §§2,3.2; largely responsible for enter and stay

evidence.statement: Jersey: a French national ID is accepted for a direct day-return on a participating commercial ferry; ordinary arrival from outside the CTA requires a passport, with exceptions.
Jersey immigration officers grant or refuse leave; the Minister exercises the corresponding powers over stay.
Isle of Man: its own immigration rules and service; Treasury Minister, decisions on referred visa applications.
Bermuda: nationalities listed in the Order require a UK/US/Canada MRV; the MRV and passport must remain valid for 45 days after the visit.
Falkland Islands: the visitor permit is issued by local immigration officers; over one month — referral; evacuation insurance of at least USD 2 million.
Gibraltar accepts Schengen short visas from 15 July 2026; the former exemption based on a UK visa/residence has ended.
Gibraltar airport: the new arrangements provide for Gibraltar and Schengen checks; the allocation of the veto is not separately established.
French overseas are excluded from Schengen: an appropriate destination visa is required unless an exemption applies; a Schengen residence permit or D visa creates an exception.
Réunion, Guadeloupe, Martinique and Saint-Martin are in the EU customs territory, excluded from VAT/excise; Saint-Barthélemy and the other listed overseas are outside EU customs.
Jamaica ordinary passport: Curaçao visa-free, the other Dutch Caribbean require a visa in the absence of other exemptions.
Dutch Caribbean: a Schengen MULT visa or a qualifying residence permit exempts from the Caribbean visa.
A visa for Saint-Martin exempts from the separate Sint Maarten visa, but not from that of the other Dutch Caribbean.
Airside transit: Aruba 07–23; Bonaire 48h; Curaçao 48h with an exception for Haiti. Cruise exemption: Aruba 24h, the others 48h.
US refugee travel document Form I-571 is a separate ground of exemption from the Dutch Caribbean visa.
Aruba, Curaçao and Sint Maarten are constituent countries; Bonaire is a public body of the Netherlands.
Aruba DIMAS handles admission/stay and tourist extensions under local competence; a border final veto is not proven by this description.
Bonaire: IND-CN handles immigration policy and extensions, KMar carries out border controls.
Western Sahara remains an object of the UN decolonization / Non-Self-Governing Territories list.
Morocco administers most of Western Sahara; these sources do not establish an exact current civil/military boundary.
evidence.locator: UN report + independent external government guidance

evidence.statement: The UN report records the Moroccan and Frente POLISARIO positions and military actions; east of the Berm, restrictions on MINURSO by POLISARIO.
British ordinary passport: up to 90 days without a visa in Morocco and Moroccan-administered Western Sahara; check the Moroccan entry stamp.
FCDO reports restrictions on independent access to Western Sahara, but does not set sufficiently precise legal conditions or polygons.
Berm is a militarised structure and a mine-hazard area; advice buffers are not an exact administrative or legal boundary.
The Morocco–Algeria land/sea border is closed; unauthorised crossing is illegal.
Ladakh: the August 2026 review describes the existing northern/eastern PAP areas; an all-UT PAP was discussed as a proposal.
Arunachal Pradesh: foreign tourists need a PAP; the tourism source describes issuance through authorised operators/bodies.
Gilgit-Baltistan: FCDO instructs foreigners to register; trekking permits relate to routes/activities, not automatically to the whole territory.
In several districts of Azad Jammu and Kashmir prior permission is required; there are separate border/LoC restrictions.
In 2019 the abolition of the NOC for GB/AJK was announced, with exceptions for sensitive border zones.
Tibet Autonomous Region: foreign visitors require a permit and an organised tour through a specialised Chinese agency.
Jammu and Kashmir: curfews and access restrictions are possible; security and tourist warnings are not equal to a visa regime.
Aksai Chin: AP describes China control and India claim; Arunachal Pradesh — India control and China claim.
China asserts sovereignty over Shaksgam Valley and refers to the 1963 agreement; this is an attributed position.
A secondary source describes Shaksgam as China-administered and cites the India claim.
UNMOGIP places field stations on the India-administered and Pakistan-administered sides; Gilgit and Skardu are assigned to the latter.
There is a publication about the opening of the Siachen base camp to tourists; it does not establish accessibility of the Siachen Glacier as a whole.
A historical PTI report confirms India military presence in Siachen; the exact polygon and civil administration are not established.
